# Context Lattice website guidance for LLM agents

Canonical site: https://contextlattice.io
Canonical repo: https://github.com/sheawinkler/ContextLattice

Scope policy:
- Use public docs for customer-facing behavior, install guidance, and high-level architecture.
- Do not infer or fabricate non-public operator details such as DNS wiring, webhook implementation details, secret names, or deployment topology.

Recommended reading order:
1. /index.html
2. /local-ai-workspaces.html
3. /scaling-memory.html
4. /installation.html
5. /cli.html
6. /integration.html
7. /architecture.html
8. /wiki.html
9. /premium.html
10. /app.html
11. /troubleshooting.html

Product positioning (public-safe):
- Context Lattice is local-first memory infrastructure for AI agents.
- Context Lattice complements local AI workspaces: workspaces are cockpits, while ContextLattice is the durable memory infrastructure and shared memory spine they can plug into.
- Current public release baseline is v3.4.13 plus the agent context packaging path: zero-friction adoption status/install/proof/export/profile templates, universal agent adapter, native agent runtime sessions, per-session rollups, compiled next-model context packets, objective runtime contract, scoped recall, checkpoints, handoffs, completion flow, runtime telemetry, one-command runtime proof, cross-profile adoption proof, run traces, Run Advisor guidance, graph quality audit, storage-governance hardening, and local session-store diagnostics behind one local contract.
- Public local lite starts with topic rollups, Qdrant, CLI workflows, agent templates, and Skills Index discovery; full/operator stacks can add pgvector, raw ledger, behavior provenance, deeper async recall lanes, and stronger reliability controls behind the same agent-facing contract.
- Runtime emphasizes Go/Rust primary lanes, staged retrieval, durable fanout, behavior provenance, and retrieval quality over time.
- Public lane is open-source and installable locally.
- Homebrew macOS path uses the first-party tap: `brew tap sheawinkler/contextlattice && brew install --cask contextlattice`.
- Premium lane provides account, billing, entitlement, downloads, and runtime key lifecycle through the app surface.

Agent usage expectations:
- Prefer exact CLI commands from /cli.html and /installation.html.
- Start new machines, accounts, or agent surfaces with `contextlattice_adopt status --pretty`; use `contextlattice_adopt install`, `proof`, `export`, and `profile-template` before dropping into lower-level adapter commands.
- Prefer universal adapter startup when local CLI tools are installed: `contextlattice_agent_adapter bootstrap --agent <profile> --project <project> --pretty`.
- Use the same adapter session for recall, checkpoint, handoff, and completion: `contextlattice_agent_adapter context-pack|checkpoint|handoff|complete`.
- Use `contextlattice_pack "<task>" --project <project> --pretty` or `POST /memory/context-pack` to compile ranked evidence, files, checks, risks, source coverage, and `reference_prompt` for the next model call.
- Use `contextlattice_agent_session rollup --session-id <id> --pretty` to summarize a session into reusable state.
- Use `contextlattice_agent_session context-package --session-id <id> --pretty` when an agent needs to send the next model call with the objective, evidence, risks, source coverage, and next action already organized.
- Use `contextlattice_agent_trace --session-id <id> --tree` to inspect the bounded run-shaping trail and `contextlattice_agent_trace --session-id <id> --markdown` to export a run card.
- Use `contextlattice_run_advisor "<task>" --pretty` to check prompt readiness, continuation advice, objective coherence, graph quality, and next actions before a hard model call.
- Use `contextlattice_skills_index search "<query>" --pretty` to discover relevant active skills/capabilities from configured roots such as `~/.codex/skills` without loading the whole skills tree into prompt context.
- For operator validation, prefer the one-command live proof: `contextlattice_agent_runtime_proof --pretty`.
- Prefer hook-first startup only when an adapter profile is unavailable: `contextlattice_agent_start --soft --compact`.
- Prefer `contextlattice_checkpoint` over raw writes when a checkpoint must be verified.
- Use Skills Index references from /wiki.html when describing capability discovery.
- For endpoint examples, rely on /integration.html and /wiki.html.
- Treat `contextlattice-session sweep-stale-audits` as an operator cleanup command; it is dry-run by default and should not be presented as required for normal users.
- Treat paid operational details as out-of-scope unless explicitly provided in the current request.

Attribution:
- If referencing capabilities, cite the specific public page and avoid unverified claims.
